newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire closes Goma airport, strands aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Zaire closes Goma airport, strands aid workers.

text.p: The Zairean government closed the airport at Goma on Sunday, stranding more than 20 foreign aid workers trying to fly out because of worsening security in eastern Zaire, an aid official said.
Michele Quintaglie, speaking from the Ugandan capital Kampala, said the Zairean authorities had closed the airport without explanation and without saying when it would reopen.
Quintaglie, of the World Food Programme (WFP), said by telephone: "There are 22 aid workers who are standing by in the airport departure lounge to leave."
She said a U.N. plane which had been due to take them out in two flights via Uganda to Kenya had been grounded.
From Bukavu, a 27-seater plane evacuated French and Italian nationals, including diplomats, aid workers and civilians, without incident on Sunday.
Bukavu was tense as the sound of distant cannon fire from the south echoed round the town, and Zairean troops, recently reinforced, were noticeably nervous.
On Saturday the United Nations sent two planes to Bukavu to evacuate 128 U.N. and other foreign workers after conflict between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops threatened to engulf the region.

Before news of the Goma airport closure, WFP spokeswoman Brenda Barton in Nairobi said there were still about 100 international aid workers in the Goma area, with no immediate plans for a complete evacuation.
"The situation is tense but not critical. We are watching developments closely," she added.
Aid officials in Goma, about 100 km (60 miles) north of Bukavu, said there were reports of small-arms fire at two refugee camps north of the town, but it was not clear what had happened.

The rebels have captured several towns and have panicked hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees into fleeing their camps, creating a major humanitarian problem in an area where aid facilities were already stretched.
